properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued August 16 at 7:58PM MDT until August 16 at 9:30PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Northern Morgan County in northeastern Colorado...
East Central Weld County in northeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 930 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Stream flows are elevated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 758 PM MDT, Minor flooding is ongoing in the advisory area.
Between 1.5 and 2 inches of rain fell earlier.

- This includes the following streams and drainages...
South Pawnee Creek, Cottonwood Creek, Baymer Creek, Igo Creek,
South Platte River, Twomile Creek, Wild Horse Creek, Pawnee
Creek, Kiowa Creek, North Pawnee Creek, Spring Creek, Wildcat
Creek, Horsetail Creek and East Prong Wildcat Creek. Flooding
impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is expected.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
New Raymer, Stoneham, Antelope Springs, Weldona, Jackson
Reservoir, Goodrich, Orchard and Buckingham.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 16 at 7:58PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 16 at 7:44PM MDT until August 16 at 8:30PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 744 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms produced heavy
rain in Fourmile Creek basin south of Highway 24. Between 1 and 3
inches of rain have fallen. Flooding impacts will continue, but no
additional rainfall is expected. Flash flooding is expected to
continue.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of West Central Teller County including the
Fourmile Creek and its tributaries south of highway 24.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Fourmile Creek and its tributaries including but not limited to Hay
Creek and Dry Creek.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued August 16 at 7:44PM MDT until August 16 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
continue to be possible over the Aspen Acres burn scar.

* WHERE...Aspen Acres Burn Scar

* WHEN...Until 10 PM MDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Aspen Acres burn scar is expected
up to and during the period of the watch. Residents near the Aspen
Acres burn scar should prepare for potential debris flow. Be sure
to stay up to date with information from local authorities. Heavy
rainfall could trigger flash flooding of low-lying areas, street
flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting
thunderstorms with heavy rainfall over the burn scar, which may
lead to flash flooding and debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Beulah, San Isabel, and highways 165 and 78 in and around the
Aspen Acres Burn Scar.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 16 at 7:37PM MDT until August 16 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 737 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain over the Southern Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Up to 1.5 inches of
rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris
flow moving through the Spring Branch and St Charles River. The
debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Southern Aspen Acres Burn
Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Southern Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Stream crossings and county roads within and immediately downstream
of the burn scar including Spring Branch, and the St Charles River
east of Beulah.

This is a second round of heavy rainfall for the very eastern edge of
the Aspen Acres Burn scar along the St Charles River.  Flooding may
occur farther downstream from the burn scar due to already saturated
conditions.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
North Saint Charles River east of Beulah, Spring Branch, Muddy
Creek and the Saint Charles River.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 16 at 7:22PM MDT until August 16 at 8:30PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
At 722 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated

Between 1.5 and 3.5 inches of rain have fallen. Flooding impacts will
continue, but no additional rainfall is expected. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, gulches, roads,
and poor drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Boyero.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Coon Creek, Rush Creek, Big Sandy Creek and Folger Gulch.
